commands.name: commands
commands.purpose: Return the machine-readable command registry with safety and composition metadata.

commands.name: version
commands.purpose: Print the canon build version.

commands.name: doctor
commands.purpose: Check whether required ADR, SPEC, and domain storage is present and parseable, and flag domain-model integrity problems (duplicate accepted titles, references to superseded or deprecated entries). Required kinds come from repository configuration; absent optional stores are healthy.

commands.name: validate
commands.purpose: Run the full corpus integrity check catalog: malformed files, duplicate ids, broken references, reciprocity, status and date validity, kind/id/directory coherence, and configured tag vocabularies. Never mutates; exit 4 on errors, or on warnings with --strict or configured strictness.

commands.name: adr validate
commands.purpose: Run the corpus integrity checks scoped to the ADR directory.

commands.name: spec validate
commands.purpose: Run the corpus integrity checks scoped to the SPEC directory.

commands.name: domain validate
commands.purpose: Run the corpus integrity checks scoped to the domain entry directory.

commands.name: config show
commands.purpose: Show the effective repository configuration resolved from .canon.jsonc (or the defaults), including discovery paths, recognized keys, and ignored unknown keys.

commands.name: config validate
commands.purpose: Validate .canon.jsonc against the configuration schema: malformed files, unsupported schema versions, invalid values, and scope mismatches are errors; unknown keys are warnings that never fail the command. Exit 4 on errors.

commands.name: adr init
commands.purpose: Create the ADR directory if it does not exist.

commands.name: spec init
commands.purpose: Create the SPEC directory if it does not exist.

commands.name: domain init
commands.purpose: Create the domain entry directory if it does not exist.

commands.name: adr new
commands.purpose: Create a new ADR markdown file with parseable metadata. ADRs capture architecture decisions.
examples: canon adr new --title "Use SQLite for local index" --status proposed --dry-run
canon adr new --title "Use SQLite for local index" --context "Need local querying" --decision "Use SQLite"

commands.name: spec new
commands.purpose: Create a new SPEC markdown file with parseable metadata. SPECs capture functional requirements.
examples: canon spec new --title "Local query index" --requirements "Return ADRs by tag." --acceptance "list --tag storage works." --dry-run

commands.name: domain new
commands.purpose: Create a new domain entry markdown file with parseable metadata. Domain entries define one canonical concept each: its definition, avoided terms with reasons, and relationships.
examples: canon domain new --title "ADR" --definition "A dated, narrowly-scoped architecture commitment." --avoid "design doc: too broad; ticket: tracks work, not decisions" --dry-run

commands.name: list
commands.purpose: List ADR, SPEC, and domain entry summaries together in deterministic order.

commands.name: adr list
commands.purpose: List ADR summaries in deterministic order.

commands.name: spec list
commands.purpose: List SPEC summaries in deterministic order.

commands.name: domain list
commands.purpose: List domain entry summaries in deterministic order.

commands.name: show
commands.purpose: Return one ADR, SPEC, or domain entry with metadata and content.

commands.name: search
commands.purpose: Search title, tags, status, kind, and markdown body across ADRs, SPECs, and domain entries.

commands.name: adr search
commands.purpose: Search title, tags, status, and markdown body across ADRs only.

commands.name: spec search
commands.purpose: Search title, tags, status, and markdown body across SPECs only.

commands.name: domain search
commands.purpose: Search title, tags, status, and markdown body across domain entries only.

commands.name: accept
commands.purpose: Mark an ADR, SPEC, or domain entry as accepted.
commands.safety: write: updates one document metadata block and appends history
examples: canon accept --id ADR-0001 --reason "Approved by the team." --dry-run

commands.name: reject
commands.purpose: Mark an ADR, SPEC, or domain entry as rejected.
commands.safety: write: updates one document metadata block and appends history
examples: canon reject --id ADR-0001 --reason "Chose a different approach." --dry-run

commands.name: supersede
commands.purpose: Mark an ADR, SPEC, or domain entry as superseded by another document of the same kind.
commands.safety: write: updates two document metadata blocks and appends history
examples: canon supersede --id ADR-0001 --by ADR-0002 --reason "Replaced by current architecture" --dry-run

commands.name: deprecate
commands.purpose: Mark an ADR, SPEC, or domain entry as deprecated without a direct replacement.
commands.safety: write: updates one document metadata block and appends history

commands.name: append
commands.purpose: Append a dated appendix section to an ADR, SPEC, or domain entry. Disabled when .canon.jsonc sets conventions.append to false.
commands.safety: write: appends markdown to one document
examples: canon append --id SPEC-0001 --title Review --body "Requirements still apply."

commands.name: skill
commands.purpose: Return the bundled skill asset catalog with names, kinds, versions, hashes, and target paths.

commands.name: skill install
commands.purpose: Install all bundled skill assets and selected subagent components into a repository.
commands.safety: write: creates skill payload files and target-specific agent files

commands.name: skill update
commands.purpose: Refresh every installed managed bundle file, refusing local modifications unless forced.
commands.safety: write: updates managed skill payload files and target-specific agent files

global_flags.name: --format
global_flags.purpose: Choose json, text, or list-only context output.

next_actions.description: Check if the ADR, SPEC, and domain directories are ready.
